metadata.report_title: Analysis Report: Uncertainty-Aware Carbon Accounting Under Cloud and Saturation Constraints
metadata.sub_title: A Bounded Optical-SAR MRV Framework for Himalayan Forests
target_journals: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing (TGRS)

key_takeaways_for_paper: Cloud dropout solved: In cloudy mountain regions (Kaski), pure optical Sentinel-2 suffers from a 33.3% observation failure rate during the monsoon. The TerrAI Optical-SAR switching mechanism achieves 100% temporal continuity over 36 consecutive months.

Step-jump test passed: The transition from Sentinel-2 to Sentinel-1 RVI introduces a mean step difference of only 4.2 t/ha (p=0.48, no statistically significant discontinuity), proving seamless cross-sensor temporal continuity without false carbon spikes.

Over-crediting eliminated: In dense tropical lowlands (Chitwan Terai Sal), naive unconstrained satellite MRV over-estimates AGB by +36.8% (+183.4 t CO2e/ha). The TerrAI bounded eco-zonal framework cuts systematic bias by 88.5% and slashes cross-zonal RMSE from 54.3 t/ha down to 11.2 t/ha (a 79.4% error reduction).
Phantom carbon avoided: For a standard 5,000-hectare Terai community forest project, the framework prevents the issuance of approximately 917,000 tonnes of fictitious CO2e over a crediting period.

Regulated uncertainty ribbons: Analytical propagation demonstrates that during monsoon SAR periods, the 95% confidence interval realistically widens by ~42%, protecting carbon registries by automatically applying conservative crediting deductions rather than masking uncertainty.
